bib.title: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks", Bojie Li (Pine AI). arXiv 2606.17929v1 [cs.AI], 16 Jun 2026. Preprint, no venue. Sole author. Code at github.com/19PINE-AI/PreAct.

COVERAGE: 39 of 39 pages, 111,644 chars, read in full, including Appendices A–H. References were skimmed for origins only. The extraction was clean.

FIT: This is a weak fit for 04-execution-boundaries. The paper is about speed and cost on repeated tasks, not safety. It has no sandbox, hook, permission gate, HITL, trust zone, rollback or canary content. Its "verify" is a screen-state predicate check plus a re-run under the benchmark's evaluator. That is correctness checking, not access control. The best home is `05-verification-loops`: check before acting, and check again before a result is stored. A secondary home is the memory or skills material in 02-context-engineering/06-memory (a store that stays honest). If the caller wants a link to 04, the only honest one is limitation L6, covered under LIMITS below.

CORE CLAIM: After a computer-using agent first succeeds at a task, PreAct compiles the run into a state-machine program. States carry screen predicates and transitions carry actions. Later runs replay it with no per-step LLM calls. It checks each state's predicate before acting and falls back to the full agent on a mismatch. A new program enters the store only if, re-run from a reset environment, the benchmark's evaluator passes it (the "verify-before-store gate").

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all paired cold/warm runs)
- **Speed:** Warm replays ran 8.5–13× faster wall-clock than a fresh agent solve. This is measured on WebArena. The Android evidence is only that a corpus hit "finishes in seconds". Replays make essentially no model calls.
- **One-time compile cost:** The verify-replay adds +162% wall time on Android (median 47 s solve, 76 s verify) and +217% on OSWorld (65 s solve, 141 s verify), per stored program.
- **Cold to warm, gate on:** AndroidWorld official-15, Gemini 3 Flash agent, 3 seeds with the corpus reset per seed. Mean 9.33 to 10.67 of 15 (+1.33), and no seed regressed.
- **Gate ablation (Table 2).** The values below are mean change in tasks solved, cold to warm, gate on versus gate off:

| Platform | Setup | Gate on | Gate off | Gate's gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AndroidWorld | Gemini, n=5 | +1.2 | −1.4 | 2.6 |
| OSWorld test_tiny (6 tasks) | Claude Sonnet 4.6, n=5 | +0.2 | −2.4 | 2.6 |
| WebArena shopping_admin (12 tasks) | n=4+4 | −4.0 | −5.75 | 1.75 |

  - Gate on beat gate off in 13 of 14 paired runs. The 14th was a tie.
  - Per-platform sign tests gave p≈0.031 on Android and OSWorld and p=0.125 on WebArena.
- **Cause of the loss:** Five programs replayed at 100% coverage yet scored 0 (Table 3). On WebArena all 48 gate-off warm replays scored 0.
- **WebArena fallback:** The gate alone rejected about 83% of compiles and left warm success at 2.0/12. Adding a cache-miss-to-agent fallback raised it to 6.25/12. That is statistically indistinguishable from Muscle-Mem (p≈0.84).
- **Cost:** About 50 hours of container time and about $30–35 in LLM spend for the whole validation.

ABLATIONS AND NULL RESULTS
- **Selector:** A plain embedding retriever matched or beat the LLM selector. Both MiniLM and bge-large reached 100% correct-family retrieval against the LLM's 75.6% (45 paraphrased queries).
- **Run-time per-state checks:** The state-machine runtime scored 11.67 against 10.6 for a flat script (+0.67 tasks, p=0.125, 3 matched seeds). This is small and not significant.
- **Guardrails:** Cold means were identical at 10.2. Warm was 11.0 with guardrails and 10.6 without (n=5).
- **Prompt additions:** None were used in production.
- **Step-budget cap:** It cost 1.8 tasks (9.8 against 11.6) for about 30% less wall time on failing runs.

QUOTES
- "a freshly compiled program enters the store only if, re-run from a clean state, an independent evaluator confirms it solved the task—catching programs that replay to their last step yet leave the task undone." (abstract, p1)
- "PreAct instead checks each state's verification predicate against the live screen before it performs the transition out of that state—observe first, then act." (§3.2, p10)
- "the program executes every action to completion (100% coverage) yet the end state does not satisfy the evaluator" (§3.3, p11)
- "many real tasks are not idempotent: re-running 'add contact Emilia Gonzalez,' 'send the email,' or 'submit the payment' duplicates the side effect rather than re-confirming the goal." (L6, p24–25)

LIMITS
- **Idempotency (L6):** The gate re-executes the program, so it assumes a resettable or idempotent environment. The paper says that for irreversible actions a side-effect-free check is needed (a read-only end-state check, a sandboxed dry-run or a transactional rollback), and it leaves that as future work. This is the one point where the paper touches execution boundaries, and only as an unsolved gap.
- **Benchmark size:** The subsets are tiny (6, 15 and 12 tasks), and the author concedes percentages depend on the denominator. Horizons are 10–30 actions. The corpus is 58 Android programs.
- **Out-of-distribution transfer:** It is harmful. A corpus built on 6 tasks scored 55.6% on 30 unseen OSWorld tasks. The cold baseline of about 67% is a single unpaired run. The cause was mis-routed retrievals.
- **WebArena:** The as-shipped gate lost to Muscle-Mem there, and only the added fallback closed the gap.
- **Compiler fidelity:** The LLM compiler is lossy on a non-trivial fraction of inputs. About 28% of Android programs lack `navigate_back`, and the verify cost scales with compile attempts.
- **Missing baselines:** There was no direct ActionEngine comparison beyond the flat-script test, and no untargeted-exploration baseline.
- **Single author:** The work is a self-reported preprint with no external replication.

NOT SHOWN: Anything about safety, permissions, prompt injection, adversarial UI, or security of replay. Also not shown are scale beyond about 60 programs, and long-horizon tasks.

BUILDS ON
- ReAct (Yao et al. 2023).
- Voyager skill library (Wang et al. 2023).
- Muscle-Mem [34], AgentRR (Feng et al. 2025), Workflow-Use (Browser-Use 2025) and ActionEngine/Compiled-AI [45, 65] as record-and-replay and compile baselines.
- Benchmarks: AndroidWorld (T3A agent) [36], OSWorld [54], WebArena (Zhou et al., ICLR 2024).
- Anthropic's Computer-Use API.
- Ideas credited: TroVE, LATM (Cai et al. 2023) and world models (Ha and Schmidhuber 2018).

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 6 (p12), "The verify-before-store gate". It shows compile, reset and re-run, then store only if replay_ok and score=1. It explains the "runs but doesn't work" failure faster than prose.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions were found. Page numbers for quotes are inferred from the printed page headers.
